[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Selection, Filtering, and Indexing in Pandas"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data manipulation in Pandas relies heavily on effective data selection, filtering, and indexing. Mastering methods like .loc, .iloc, and the standard indexing operator (__getitem__) is essential for extracting precise subsets of data from DataFrames and Series."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. The Standard Indexing Operator (__getitem__)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The bracket notation df[item] primarily selects columns in a DataFrame or elements in a Series. While convenient for simple column extraction, it can be ambiguous when mixed with rows and slices."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd

# Sample DataFrame
data = {'Name': ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie'],
        'Age': [25, 30, 35],
        'City': ['New York', 'London', 'Paris']}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Selecting a single column
ages = df['Age']
print(ages)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Label-based Indexing with .loc"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The .loc accessor is primarily label-based. You specify rows and columns by their index and column labels. It also accepts boolean arrays for filtering conditions."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Selecting a specific row and column by label
print(df.loc[0, 'Name'])

# Selecting a slice of rows and multiple columns
print(df.loc[0:1, ['Name', 'City']])"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Integer-based Indexing with .iloc"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The .iloc accessor is strictly integer-position based, similar to Python list slicing. It means you use 0-based integer indexes regardless of what the row labels or column names are."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Selecting the first row and all columns
print(df.iloc[0, :])

# Selecting rows from index 0 to 2 (exclusive) and columns 0 to 2 (exclusive)
print(df.iloc[0:2, 0:2])"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Advanced Filtering with Boolean Masks"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Filtering data based on conditions involves creating a boolean mask and passing it into .loc or the indexing operator. This allows for dynamic querying of your dataset."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Filtering rows where Age is greater than 28
filtered_df = df.loc[df['Age'] > 28]
print(filtered_df)"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use df['col'] for quick column extraction."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use df.loc[row_label, col_label] for precise label-based lookups."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use df.iloc[row_idx, col_idx] for strict integer-position slicing."}]
